# Graft example: landing-page

This site is operated by editing files — there is no dashboard.
There are two equivalent interfaces: edit files directly, or use the MCP server.

## MCP server (preferred for agents)

`pnpm mcp` serves this site's content tools over stdio. It is already
registered in the repo-root `.mcp.json` as `graft-landing-page`:

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "graft-landing-page": {
          "command": "pnpm",
          "args": ["--filter", "landing-page", "--silent", "mcp"]
        }
      }
    }

Tools: `list_collections`, `describe_schema`, `list_content`, `get_content`,
`search_content` (full-text search across collections; each hit carries the
`sourcePath` of the file to edit), `write_content` (validates, writes the MDX
file, compiles — one call), `explain_error`. Every failure returns JSON with a
`fix` — do what it says. Writes land as plain files under `content/`; commit
them like any other change.

Remote agents (no stdio): the same tools are served over Streamable HTTP at
`POST /api/mcp` while the app is running (`pnpm dev`). Stateless, JSON
responses; set `GRAFT_MCP_TOKEN` to require a bearer token.

## How to change content (by hand)

1. Edit or add MDX under `content/pages/`. Frontmatter must satisfy the
   `pages` collection in `graft.config.ts` (title: string; tagline?: string;
   order?: number; slug: kebab-case, defaults to the filename).
   `order` is the nav position (ascending; home=1 — give a new page the next
   free number).
2. Run `pnpm compile` (the `graft compile` CLI). It validates every file and
   reports exactly what was added/changed/removed. Validation errors include a
   `fix` field — do what it says and re-run. `pnpm watch` (`graft dev`)
   recompiles on every save instead.
3. The running app (`pnpm dev`, http://localhost:3000) serves the new content
   on the next request. Home is the `home` slug; everything else is `/<slug>`.
4. Commit the change — git is the version history and the source of truth.

## How to add an image (or any binary)

1. Upload it: `pnpm exec graft asset put <file> [key]` (e.g.
   `graft asset put assets/hero.svg pages/home/hero.svg`). Uses the `S3_*`
   env from the repo-root `.env`; the command prints the frontmatter snippet.
2. Reference it from an `asset` field in frontmatter:

       image:
         key: pages/home/hero.svg
         alt: describe the image

3. `pnpm compile`. The app resolves the key to a URL at render time
   (presigned GET; set `S3_PUBLIC_URL` for stable public URLs).

## Functions (typed server logic)

Functions are code in `graft.config.ts` (`defineFunction`) exported via
`export const functions = { … }`, served while the app runs at:

    POST /api/fn/<name>        body: JSON object of the input fields
                               (empty body = {})

Success is `{ data: … }`; failure is GraftError JSON — `fix` says what to do,
`details.issues` lists field violations, and `explain_error` knows every code.

Registered functions:

- `pageStats` — query, no input; returns the live page slugs on the branch.
- `submitContact` — mutation, `public: true`; input `{ email, message? }`;
  stores a row in the `submissions` collection (the home-page contact form
  posts here). Rate-limited: 5/min per caller.
- `listSubmissions` — query, gated by `requireScopes("submissions:read")`;
  input `{ limit? }`; anonymous or unscoped callers get 401.
- `searchSubmissions` — query, same gate; input `{ query, limit? }`; full-text
  search over submissions, best match first.
- `deleteSubmission` — mutation, `destructive: true`; input `{ id }`; requires
  the `submissions:admin` scope AND human approval (see below).

To add a function: define input with the same `field.*` builders collections
use, write the handler against the standard context
(`{ input, db, actor, branch, request, correlationId }`), and add it to the
exported `functions` record. Mutations reject anonymous callers by default —
set `public: true` only when anonymous calls are the point (e.g. a form), or
supply an `access` rule (it replaces the default entirely). Mark anything
that deletes or irreversibly overwrites data `destructive: true`.

## Audit, rate limits, and human approval

Every function invocation writes an `audit_log` row (actor, correlationId,
git SHA, status, duration) — the `x-graft-correlation-id` response header is
the key into it.

Rate limits are per caller per function (your actor id; your IP when
anonymous). 429 responses carry `Retry-After`; every attempt counts, including
rejected ones, so back off — do not tight-loop retries.

Destructive functions never run directly. The workflow:

1. Call it normally → 403 `DESTRUCTIVE_OP_REQUIRES_APPROVAL` with
   `details.approvalId`. A pending approval (function + exact input) is filed.
2. A HUMAN reviews it: `pnpm exec graft approvals` lists pending ones;
   `graft approve <id>` or `graft deny <id>` decides. Agents must not run
   these themselves — ask the operator and wait.
3. Once approved, retry the EXACT same request with the header
   `x-graft-approval: <id>`. Approvals are one-shot and bound to that exact
   input; any drift is `APPROVAL_INVALID` with the reason in details.

## Authentication (who is calling a function)

Callers are identified by `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, resolved by
`@graft/auth` (`app/api/fn/[name]/route.ts`). Two kinds of tokens work:

- **JWTs from this app's Better Auth instance** (`lib/auth.ts`, mounted at
  `/api/auth`). Sign in (`POST /api/auth/sign-in/email`), then mint a JWT at
  `GET /api/auth/token` — it carries `scope: "submissions:read"`. The same
  verifier path accepts any trusted OIDC issuer (company IdP, Vercel
  Connect/Passport).
- **`GRAFT_DEV_TOKEN`** from the repo-root `.env` — a static local-dev
  credential mapped to a human actor with `submissions:read`.

No header → anonymous. A bad/expired token is `TOKEN_INVALID` (401) with the
reason in `details` — fix the token; do not retry anonymously.

## Operational data (db-authoritative collections)

`submissions` has `authority: "db-authoritative"`: Postgres owns its rows and
the ONLY way in or out is through functions (`insertRecord` / `listRecords`
inside handlers — validated against the collection schema both directions).
Do not create `content/submissions/` files and do not use `write_content`
for it — both fail with AUTHORITY_MISMATCH and point you back here.

## Search

Full-text search is built in (Postgres, websearch syntax: plain words,
`"quoted phrases"`, `or`, `-exclusions`):

- **Content:** the `search_content` MCP tool, or `getGraft().searchContent(...)`
  from `lib/graft.ts` in server components. It searches the compiled index —
  results are as fresh as the last compile — and ranks slug matches over
  frontmatter over body. Hits carry a highlighted `snippet` and `sourcePath`.
- **Operational data:** per collection, through gated functions only
  (`searchRecords` inside a handler; `searchSubmissions` here).

## How to change the schema

Edit `graft.config.ts` (fields are built with `field.string()`,
`field.number({ optional: true })`, …), then update the MDX files to match and
run `pnpm compile`. Reads are typed from this file — no codegen step.

## Layout of this app

- `graft.config.ts` — collections (the schema; single source of truth)
- `content/pages/*.mdx` — the authored documents
- `lib/graft.ts` — the typed read client (`getContent`, `listContent`,
  `searchContent`)
- `app/page.tsx`, `app/[slug]/page.tsx` — routes that render documents
- `pnpm compile` / `pnpm watch` — project content into Postgres (the `graft` CLI)

## Rules

- Never write to the database directly; it is a derived index. Files win.
- Slugs are kebab-case (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens).
- `DATABASE_URL` comes from the repo-root `.env`.
